file_roles.evidence: The shared forbidGenerationOverrides(targetRCL, forUpdate, addedGeneratedColumns) is deleted outright. The commit message names it as the defect: 'the former way of checking for illegal override of generated columns in the presence of an explicit target column list failed to look below the top level UnionNode in a table constructor'.

The call into the broken check is removed: '// don't allow overriding of generation clauses' and 'forbidGenerationOverrides( targetColumnList, false, null );' are both deleted, so INSERT now goes through the general no-target-list path. This is the 'insert into t(b,a) values (default,1), (default,2)' case in the report.

A private, UPDATE-only copy of forbidGenerationOverrides is added and the call loses its now-meaningless boolean, 'forbidGenerationOverrides(resultSet.getResultColumns(), addedGeneratedColumns)'. The body is the same logic moved down from the shared parent; UPDATE behaviour is unchanged.

rationale: The reporter gives the failing statements and the two messages, 'ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException' in an insane build and 'ASSERT FAILED More columns in result column list than in base table' in a sane one, but pastes no stack trace, so no symptom or log file can be placed. The commit message states the mechanism plainly, and the diff matches: the broken check is deleted from the shared parent and its INSERT call site, while UPDATE keeps a private copy. Two gold files are therefore causal and the third is a code move.
notes: The fix for both reported symptoms is a deletion, and the only file that gains code, UpdateNode, is the one labelled refactor. The same commit also closes DERBY-4448, so the gold set covers two issues.
